FROMGIT: mm, drm/i915: mark pinned shmemfs pages as unevictable The i915 driver uses shmemfs to allocate backing storage for gem objects. These shmemfs pages can be pinned (increased ref count) by shmem_read_mapping_page_gfp(). When a lot of pages are pinned, vmscan wastes a lot of time scanning these pinned pages. In some extreme case, all pages in the inactive anon lru are pinned, and only the inactive anon lru is scanned due to inactive_ratio, the system cannot swap and invokes the oom-killer. Mark these pinned pages as unevictable to speed up vmscan. Export pagevec API check_move_unevictable_pages(). This patch was inspired by Chris Wilson's change [1]. CHROMIUM: iio: cros_ec_sensors: track wakeups based on _WAKEUP flag There are a few cases where cros_ec sensors might want to wake the AP -- particularly with a "significant motion" event. Currently, the main cros_ec device treats all EC_MKBP_EVENT_SENSOR_FIFO interrupts as wakeup events in its ISR, but this is not the right way to do it. There are plenty of non-wakeup sensor events that occur, and if we treat them as wakeups, this may disturb the wakeup_count and interrupt entry into system suspend (e.g., S3). So instead, let's log the wakeup event in the cros_ec_sensors driver, where we parse the MOTIONSENSE flags. After we do this, it's safe to start ignoring EC_MKBP_EVENT_SENSOR_FIFO events in the parent device, with respect to wakeups. BUG=b:118685087 TEST=suspend_stress_test on scarlet; find a device that supports "significant motion" and ensure it still increases 'wakeup_count' Change-Id: Ibc162fe4d0fc335d525595e27d2d377cd4104e51 Signed-off-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1319994 Reviewed-by: Ravi Chandra Sadineni <ravisadineni@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: cros-ec: don't report EC_MKBP_EVENT_SENSOR_FIFO as wakeup [Adapted for upstream here: https://lore.kernel.org/patchwork/patch/1008110/ https://lkml.kernel.org/r/20181108024939.174321-2-briannorris@chromium.org but much of this was refactored and moved to drivers/platform/chrome/, so I don't bother with a direct BACKPORT. Note that patch 1 of 2 in that series doesn't really apply to this kernel, since we don't have the incorrect documentation here, and we were already ignoring 'ret == 0' cases from cros_ec_get_next_event().] EC_MKBP_EVENT_SENSOR_FIFO events can be triggered for a variety of reasons, and there are very few cases in which they should be treated as wakeup interrupts (particularly, when a certain MOTIONSENSE_MODULE_FLAG_* is set, but this is not even supported in the mainline cros_ec_sensor driver yet). Most of the time, they are benign sensor readings. In any case, the top-level cros_ec device doesn't know enough to determine that they should wake the system, and so it should not report the event. This would be the job of the cros_ec_sensors driver to parse. This patch adds checks to cros_ec_get_next_event() such that it doesn't signal 'wakeup' for events of type EC_MKBP_EVENT_SENSOR_FIFO. This patch is particularly relevant on devices like Scarlet (Rockchip RK3399 tablet, known as Acer Chromebook Tab 10), where the EC firmware reports sensor events much more frequently. This was causing /sys/power/wakeup_count to increase very frequently, often needlessly interrupting our ability to suspend the system. crash: Generate ACPI APEI BERT Dumps ACPI/APEI is designed to report H/W errors. Under normal circumstances, when a hardware error occurs, kernel will be notified and recovered it if possible. But sometimes the system is unable to process errors and firmware may choose to reset directly without notifying kernel or system might experience an uncontrolled reset. BERT Table can be used to capture such un-notified hardware errors that occurred in the previous boot. The BERT table is reported by coreboot firmware and read by kernel during system boot. The ACPI sysfs interface provides a way to read BERT table via /sys/firmware/acpi/tables/BERT and BERT data via /sys/firmware/acpi/tables/data/BERT from userspace. (Upstream kernel commit 7dae6326ed76431653793df0388b3a404de1217e) For more information about BERT, please refer to ACPI Specification, section 18.3.1 (https://www.uefi.org/sites/default/files/resources/ACPI%206_2_A_Sept29.pdf). The CL creates Boot Error Record Table Dump(BERT table+BERT data) into a single file in case of unhandled firmware errors that occurred in the previous boot. The BERT collector should not have PII issues as it collects only SOC platform information at generic hardware components level. BUG=b:70403874 TEST=emerge-$BOARD crash-reporter TEST="FEATURES=test emerge-$BOARD crash-reporter" and verify following unit tests: 1.No bert table 2.Bert with no consent to dump 3.Bert with bad test data with consent to dump 4.Bert Dump with dummy test table and data created Change-Id: Ib8d883dd5b874b72a6997ed47a19599f42bf9903 Signed-off-by: Nataraj Deshpande <nataraj.deshpande@intel.com> Signed-off-by: Dmytro Chystiakov <dmytro.chystiakov@intel.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/767107 Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org>

This CL does that to remove sensor related code from arc-network.conf.
